body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

items: at the mercy of the present

blocks.title: Why We Still Read the Classics
paras: **It is fashionable** to ask why anyone should read books written centuries ago. **The answer is not that they are good for us**, like cod-liver oil, **but that they are rarely only what they seem**. **For all their** archaic dress, they pose questions we **have not outgrown**: what we owe the dead, what love costs, how power corrupts.

**Not least**, a classic **rewards re-reading**. **Were** we to read only what is new, we **would be** forever **at the mercy of** the present. **That said**, the canon is not **sacred**; it has been **revised** and **will be again**. **What matters is** not reverence **but** conversation.

items.q: The editorial says classics are good for us like medicine.
items.why: not that they are good for us.

items.q: The editorial says the canon is unchangeable.
The editorial concludes that conversation matters more than reverence.

blocks.body: *That said* e *For all their* funcionam como **dobradiças** do argumento. *Not least* não significa “nem um pouco”, mas “em especial”.
*Not least* ≠ *at least*. *At least* = pelo menos; *not least* = sobretudo.

items.s: ___ all their archaic dress, they pose current questions. (for)
That ___ , the canon is not sacred. (said)
What matters is not reverence ___ conversation. (but)

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence editorial defending reading something old or difficult (a classic, a hard book), using For all…, Not least, That said and What matters is not… but….
blocks.model: It is fashionable to dismiss difficult books. For all their demands, they reward patience. Not least, they stretch our attention. That said, no one should read out of duty. What matters is not completion but curiosity. Pick one, and begin.
